docs.title: Calendary
docs.text:
Calendary is a lightweight, framework-agnostic PHP library for resolving calendar availability, busy periods and bookable time slots.

It lets your application define when a resource can be available, provide the periods when it is already occupied, and query the resulting calendar.

use Eril\Calendary\Calendary;

$calendar = Calendary::load([
    'weekly' => [
        1 => [['09:00', '12:00'], ['14:00', '18:00']],
        2 => [['09:00', '18:00']],
        3 => [['09:00', '18:00']],
        4 => [['09:00', '18:00']],
        5 => [['09:00', '17:00']],
    ],
]);

$calendar
    ->timezone('Atlantic/Cape_Verde')
    ->duration(60)
    ->interval(30)
    ->busy([
        ['2026-10-05 10:00'],
    ]);

$result = $calendar
    ->query()
    ->available()
    ->availableSlots()
    ->between('2026-10-05', '2026-10-09');

docs.title: Why Calendary?
docs.text:
Scheduling usually combines two different concerns:

  1. Availability — when a resource is allowed to work or receive bookings.
  2. Occupancy — when that resource is already unavailable.

Calendary keeps these concepts separate from your database and application infrastructure.

Application
    ↓
availability + busy periods
    ↓
Calendary
    ↓
resolved days and slots
    ↓
Application / API / UI

Calendary does not require an ORM, database, HTTP framework or external calendar provider.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Recurring weekly availability
  • Date-specific availability
  • Busy periods
  • Days off and holidays
  • Configurable slot duration
  • Configurable slot interval
  • Timezone-aware resolution
  • Day and slot filtering
  • Output field selection
  • Array and JSON serialization
  • Framework-independent architecture

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
composer require eril/calendary

Calendary requires PHP 8.2 or later.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Start with Getting Started to create your first calendar.

docs.text:
Calendary::load(array $schedule): Calendary
````

Creates a calendar from weekly and date-specific availability.

### `timezone()`

```php
$calendar->timezone(string|DateTimeZone $timezone): Calendary

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
Day, Slot and Range implement:

Eril\Calendary\Contracts\Result

The contract provides:

public function toArray(): array;

public function toJson(int $flags = 0): string;

and extends PHP's JsonSerializable.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text:
Availability defines when a resource can be available.

It does not mean that every generated slot will actually be available. Busy periods are applied later during calendar resolution.

docs.title: Loading Availability
docs.text:
Calendary::load() expects availability already normalized into the Calendary schedule format.

$calendar = Calendary::load([
    'weekly' => [
        1 => [['09:00', '12:00'], ['14:00', '18:00']],
        2 => [['09:00', '18:00']],
        // weekday => [[start, end], ...]
    ],

    'dates' => [
        '2026-10-08' => [['10:00', '14:00']],
        // date => [[start, end], ...]
    ],
]);

weekly uses ISO weekdays (1 = Monday, 7 = Sunday), while dates uses YYYY-MM-DD keys.

Calendary does not fetch availability from a database or ORM directly. Your application should map its data into this structure before calling load().

For example:

$weekly = [];

foreach ($rows as $row) {
    $weekly[$row['weekday']][] = [
        $row['start_time'],
        $row['end_time'],
    ];
}

$calendar = Calendary::load([
    'weekly' => $weekly,
]);

docs.title: Weekly Availability
docs.text:
Use weekly for recurring availability:

$calendar = Calendary::load([
    'weekly' => [
        1 => [
            ['09:00', '12:00'],
            ['14:00', '18:00'],
        ],

        2 => [
            ['09:00', '18:00'],
        ],
    ],
]);
````

A weekday may contain multiple availability periods.

## Date-Specific Availability

Use `dates` for exceptions:

```php
$calendar = Calendary::load([
    'weekly' => [
        4 => [['09:00', '18:00']],
    ],

    'dates' => [
        '2026-10-08' => [
            ['10:00', '14:00'],
        ],
    ],
]);

Date-specific availability completely replaces weekly availability for that date.

Therefore, October 8 is available from 10:00 to 14:00, not from 09:00 to 18:00.

docs.title: Explicitly Closing a Date
docs.text:
An empty date-specific definition closes that date:

'dates' => [
    '2026-10-08' => [],
]

This is different from simply omitting the date.

If the date is omitted, Calendary falls back to the weekly schedule.

docs.title: Resolution Precedence
docs.text:
Calendary resolves availability in this order:

holiday / day off
        ↓
date-specific availability
        ↓
weekly availability
        ↓
generate slots
        ↓
apply busy periods

A holiday or day off closes the date regardless of its weekly or date-specific availability.

docs.title: Days Off
docs.text:
$calendar->daysOff([
    '2026-10-07',
]);

A resolved day will have the status:

day_off

docs.title: Holidays
docs.text:
$calendar->holidays([
    '2026-12-25',
    '2027-01-01',
]);

A resolved holiday has the status:

holiday

docs.title: Slot Duration
docs.text:
$calendar->duration(60);

For availability from 09:00 to 12:00:

09:00 - 10:00
10:00 - 11:00
11:00 - 12:00

docs.title: Slot Interval
docs.text:
The interval determines how frequently a candidate slot begins.

$calendar
    ->duration(60)
    ->interval(30);

The same 09:00 to 12:00 availability produces:

09:00 - 10:00
09:30 - 10:30
10:00 - 11:00
10:30 - 11:30
11:00 - 12:00

A candidate slot is included only when its complete duration fits inside the availability period.

docs.title: Timezone
docs.text:
$calendar->timezone('Atlantic/Cape_Verde');

You may also provide a DateTimeZone:

$calendar->timezone(
    new DateTimeZone('Atlantic/Cape_Verde')
);

If no timezone is configured, PHP's current default timezone is used.

docs.title: Busy Time
docs.text:
Busy periods represent time that would otherwise be available but cannot currently be used.

They are normally populated from appointments, reservations or external calendar events.

docs.title: Busy Datetime
docs.text:
$calendar->busy([
    ['2026-10-05 10:00'],
]);
````

When only a start datetime is supplied, Calendary uses the configured
duration.

With:

```php
$calendar->duration(60);

the busy period is:

10:00 - 11:00

docs.title: Explicit Busy Period
docs.text:
Provide both boundaries when the occupied period has an explicit duration:

$calendar->busy([
    [
        '2026-10-05 14:20',
        '2026-10-05 15:40',
    ],
]);

Any generated slot overlapping that period becomes busy.

docs.title: Busy Date
docs.text:
A date without a time blocks the entire date:

$calendar->busy([
    ['2026-10-06'],
]);

docs.title: Break Time
docs.text:
breakTime() defines additional unavailable time after a booking whose end is inferred by Calendary.

```php id="8x8rpb" $calendar ->duration(60) ->breakTime(15) ->busy([ ['2026-10-05 09:00'], ]); 

The booking itself still lasts 60 minutes:

```text id="p5v1rp"
09:00 ─────── booking ─────── 10:00

but the calendar remains unavailable for another 15 minutes:

```text id="g6hmhn" 09:00 ─────── booking ─────── 10:00 ─ break ─ 10:15 

The effective busy period is therefore `[09:00, 10:15)`.

Break time does not change the duration of generated slots.

### Explicit Busy Periods

Break time is only applied when Calendary needs to infer the end of a busy period.

When both the start and end are explicitly provided, the period is respected exactly as given:

```php id="eflgx7"
$calendar
    ->breakTime(15)
    ->busy([
        ['2026-10-05 09:00', '2026-10-05 10:30'],
    ]);

The busy period remains [09:00, 10:30). It is not extended to 10:45.

Whole-day busy entries are also not extended.

Busy definition Resolution [date] Blocks the whole day [datetime] Uses duration + breakTime [start, end] Uses the exact explicit period

docs.title: Period Overlap
docs.text:
Calendary uses half-open intervals:

[start, end)

For example:

busy: 10:00 - 11:00
slot: 11:00 - 12:00

These periods do not overlap.

But:

busy: 10:30 - 11:30
slot: 11:00 - 12:00

does overlap.

docs.title: Multi-Day Busy Periods
docs.text:
Explicit busy periods may cross date boundaries:

$calendar->busy([
    [
        '2026-10-05 18:00',
        '2026-10-08 09:00',
    ],
]);

Calendary checks period overlap for every resolved date affected by the busy period.

docs.title: Busy vs Days Off
docs.text:
Busy time and closed dates represent different concepts.

Use busy() when availability exists but time has become occupied.

Use daysOff() or holidays() when the schedule itself should not operate on that date.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install Calendary using Composer:

composer require eril/calendary
````

Then import the main class:

```php
use Eril\Calendary\Calendary;

docs.title: Creating a Calendar
docs.text:
Availability is loaded using Calendary::load():

$calendar = Calendary::load([
    'weekly' => [
        1 => [['09:00', '12:00'], ['14:00', '18:00']],
        2 => [['09:00', '18:00']],
        3 => [['09:00', '18:00']],
        4 => [['09:00', '18:00']],
        5 => [['09:00', '17:00']],
    ],
]);

Weekly availability uses ISO-8601 weekdays:

Value Day 1 Monday 2 Tuesday 3 Wednesday 4 Thursday 5 Friday 6 Saturday 7 Sunday

docs.title: Configure the Calendar
docs.text:
$calendar
    ->timezone('Atlantic/Cape_Verde')
    ->duration(60)
    ->interval(30);

duration() controls the length of each generated slot.

interval() controls the distance between candidate slot start times.

When no interval is configured, the duration is used as the interval.

docs.title: Query a Date
docs.text:
$day = $calendar
    ->query()
    ->on('2026-10-05');

You can then inspect the resolved result:

$day->status();
$day->available();
$day->slots();
$day->availableSlots();

Or serialize it:

$array = $day->toArray();

$json = $day->toJson();

docs.title: Query a Range
docs.text:
$range = $calendar
    ->query()
    ->between(
        '2026-10-05',
        '2026-10-12'
    );

Ranges are inclusive.

docs.title: A Typical Availability Query
docs.text:
For an API or booking interface, you may want only open days and available slots:

$result = $calendar
    ->query()
    ->available()
    ->availableSlots()
    ->select('date', 'slots')
    ->between(
        '2026-10-05',
        '2026-10-12'
    );

return $result->toArray();

The same calendar can later be used to validate a requested booking:

$day = $calendar
    ->query()
    ->on('2026-10-05');

if (!$day->isAvailable('10:00')) {
    throw new DomainException(
        'The requested time is not available.'
    );
}

docs.title: Querying
docs.text:
Calendar resolution begins with:

$query = $calendar->query();
````

Queries do not modify the underlying calendar definition.

## Single Date

```php
$day = $calendar
    ->query()
    ->on('2026-10-05');

Returns a Day.

docs.title: Week
docs.text:
$week = $calendar
    ->query()
    ->weekOf('2026-10-07');

weekOf() returns the ISO week containing the date:

Monday → Sunday

docs.title: Range
docs.text:
$range = $calendar
    ->query()
    ->between(
        '2026-10-01',
        '2026-10-31'
    );

Ranges are inclusive.

docs.title: Filtering by Status
docs.text:
open closed full day_off holiday

$result = $calendar
    ->query()
    ->status('open')
    ->between($from, $to);

Multiple statuses may be provided:

$result = $calendar
    ->query()
    ->status('open', 'full')
    ->between($from, $to);

docs.title: Day Statuses
docs.text:
Each resolved day has one of the following statuses:

Status Meaning open The day has at least one available slot. closed No availability schedule applies to the day. full Availability exists, but all generated slots are busy. day_off The day was explicitly marked as a day off. holiday The day was explicitly marked as a holiday.

The main distinction between closed and full is that a closed day has no applicable availability, while a full day has availability but no remaining available slots.

docs.title: Available Days
docs.text:
$result = $calendar
    ->query()
    ->available()
    ->between($from, $to);

available() keeps only days containing at least one available slot.

docs.title: Available Slots
docs.text:
$result = $calendar
    ->query()
    ->availableSlots()
    ->between($from, $to);

This removes busy slots from returned Day objects.

It does not recalculate the original status of the day.

docs.title: Selecting Fields
docs.text:
$result = $calendar
    ->query()
    ->select('date', 'status')
    ->between($from, $to);

Available fields are:

date
weekday
available
status
slots

select() controls serialization only.

It does not remove information from the Day object.

$day = $calendar
    ->query()
    ->select('status')
    ->on('2026-10-05');

$day->toArray();
// ['status' => 'open']

$day->date();
$day->slots();
$day->available();

All domain methods remain available.

docs.title: Combining Filters
docs.text:
Query operations can be combined:

$result = $calendar
    ->query()
    ->status('open')
    ->availableSlots()
    ->select('date', 'slots')
    ->between(
        '2026-10-05',
        '2026-10-12'
    );

This means:

  1. keep open days;
  2. remove busy slots;
  3. serialize only the date and slots;
  4. resolve the requested range.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Calendary returns result objects rather than raw arrays.

The primary result types are:

Day
Slot
Range
````

Each implements the `Result` contract and supports:

```php
$result->toArray();
$result->toJson();

They are also JSON serializable.

docs.title: Day
docs.text:
A Day represents the resolved state of one calendar date.

$day->date();
$day->weekday();

$day->status();
$day->available();

$day->slots();
$day->availableSlots();

$day->isAvailable('10:00');

docs.title: Day Statuses
Slot
docs.text:
A Slot represents one generated time period.

$slot->start();
$slot->end();

$slot->status();
$slot->available();

Slot statuses are:

available
busy

Constants:

Slot::AVAILABLE;
Slot::BUSY;

start() and end() return DateTimeImmutable.

docs.title: Range
docs.text:
A Range contains resolved days for a requested date range.

$range->from();
$range->to();
$range->days();

The requested range boundaries remain unchanged when filters are used.

For example:

$range = $calendar
    ->query()
    ->status('open')
    ->between(
        '2026-10-01',
        '2026-10-31'
    );

from() and to() still represent the requested October range, while days() contains only matching days.

docs.title: Serialization
docs.text:
$data = $result->toArray();

Or:

$json = $result->toJson();

You may also use normal JSON serialization:

$json = json_encode(
    $result,
    JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR
);
